# Snapshot schema

qbitflow keeps two databases.

**`/data/qbitflow.db`** is on disk and holds only configuration, rules and run
history. It is the thing to back up.

**The snapshot** is an in-memory SQLite database rebuilt from scratch on every
refresh cycle and swapped in atomically. Every rule in a cycle evaluates against
the same immutable copy, so two rules can never disagree about the state of a
torrent. Losing it costs one refresh and nothing else.

Everything derived -- normalized path keys, sizes in gigabytes, days since a
timestamp, the mount a torrent's save path resolves to -- is a real column computed
once at ingest rather than an expression evaluated per row per rule. That is what
makes a fifty-rule cycle over ten thousand torrents take well under a second.

Tables readable from advanced (raw SQL) mode:

- `media_files`
- `media_items`
- `play_counts`
- `source_status`
- `storage_paths`
- `torrent_files`
- `torrents`
- `watch_history`

Anything else -- writes, attaches, pragmas, other databases -- is refused by a
SQLite authorizer callback, not by string inspection, so there is no phrasing that
gets around it.

## DDL

```sql
CREATE TABLE media_files (
    media_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    path          TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    path_key      TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    media_key     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    parent_key    TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    size_bytes    INTEGER
)

CREATE TABLE media_items (
    id                     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    -- Identity across services: type + normalized title + year, so the same film
    -- known to both Plex and Jellyfin is one row with their counts combined.
    match_key              TEXT    NOT NULL,
    title                  TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    title_key              TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    media_type             TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    year                   INTEGER,
    rating                 REAL,
    audience_rating        REAL,
    user_rating            REAL,
    content_rating         TEXT,
    genres                 TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT ',',
    duration_ms            INTEGER,
    duration_minutes       REAL,
    added_at               INTEGER,
    days_since_added       REAL,
    series_title           TEXT,
    season                 INTEGER,
    episode                INTEGER,
    source_names           TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT ',',
    -- Rolled up from watch_history across every source that reported on it.
    watch_total            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    last_watched_at        INTEGER,
    days_since_last_watched REAL,
    -- 0..1 rank of watch_total among items of the same media type. "Unpopular
    -- for a film" and "unpopular for a TV episode" are different bars.
    watch_popularity       REAL
)

CREATE TABLE play_counts (
    media_item_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    total_plays       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    source_count      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    last_played_at    INTEGER,
    days_since_played REAL,
    plays_week        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    plays_month       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    plays_year        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    plays_all         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
)

CREATE TABLE source_status (
    source_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,
    source_name TEXT    NOT NULL,
    kind        TEXT    NOT NULL,
    fetched_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
    ok          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    error       TEXT,
    row_count   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
)

CREATE TABLE storage_paths (
    name              TEXT    NOT NULL,
    name_key          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    path              TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    path_key          TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    -- 0 when the path is missing or unmountable. Every numeric column below is
    -- then 0, so a rule reading it gets a defined answer instead of an error.
    available         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    error             TEXT,
    total_bytes       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    used_bytes        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    free_bytes        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    total_gb          REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    used_gb           REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    free_gb           REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    used_percent      REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    free_percent      REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    filesystem        TEXT,
    mountpoint        TEXT,
    folder_size_bytes INTEGER,
    folder_size_gb    REAL
)

CREATE TABLE torrents (
    source_id            INTEGER NOT NULL,
    source_name          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    hash                 TEXT    NOT NULL,
    name                 TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    name_lower           TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    category             TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    category_lower       TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    -- Comma-wrapped (',hd,seed,') so a tag test is a LIKE on ',tag,' and cannot
    -- match a longer tag that merely contains it.
    tags                 TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT ',',
    tag_count            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    save_path            TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    save_path_key        TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    content_path         TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    content_path_key     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    -- Release name reduced to a comparable form; see qbitflow.snapshot.mediakey.
    media_key            TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    state                TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    is_complete          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    is_paused            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    size                 INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    size_gb              REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    total_size           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    downloaded           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    uploaded             INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    uploaded_gb          REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    amount_left          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    progress             REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    ratio                REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    download_limit       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    upload_limit         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    download_speed       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    upload_speed         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    num_seeds            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    num_leechs           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    num_complete         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    num_incomplete       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    priority             INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    active_time_seconds  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    active_time_days     REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    seeding_time_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    seeding_time_days    REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    eta_seconds          INTEGER,
    availability         REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    tracker              TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    -- Epoch seconds; NULL means never, which is not the same as 1970.
    added_on             INTEGER,
    completion_on        INTEGER,
    last_activity        INTEGER,
    last_seen_complete   INTEGER,
    days_since_added     REAL,
    days_since_completed REAL,
    days_since_activity  REAL,
    force_start          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    auto_managed         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    super_seeding        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    -- Storage attribution: the mount this torrent's save path sits on, so a
    -- disk-pressure rule does not have to hard-code a mount name.
    mount                TEXT,
    mount_total_bytes    INTEGER,
    mount_free_bytes     INTEGER,
    mount_used_percent   REAL,
    mount_free_percent   REAL,
    -- Media match, filled in by the matcher. NULL means no library item matched.
    media_item_id        INTEGER,
    match_confidence     REAL,
    match_strategy       TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (source_id, hash)
)

CREATE TABLE torrent_files (
    source_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    torrent_hash  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    idx           INTEGER NOT NULL,
    path          TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    path_key      TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    media_key     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    size          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    size_gb       REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    progress      REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    priority      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
)

CREATE TABLE watch_history (
    source_id       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    source_name     TEXT    NOT NULL,
    media_item_id   INTEGER,
    source_item_id  TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    title           TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    title_key       TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    media_type      TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    play_count      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    last_played_at  INTEGER,
    days_since_played REAL,
    watched_seconds INTEGER,
    -- Per-window counts, NULL where the source does not expose that window.
    plays_week      INTEGER,
    plays_month     INTEGER,
    plays_year      INTEGER,
    plays_all       INTEGER
)

```
